tasks.short: Choose and order diagnostic tests, interpret results and document their clinical meaning.

steps.what: Retrieve the patient context and relevant diagnostic testing guidance
Determine appropriate diagnostic or laboratory tests and their clinical indications
Enter the chosen tests, indications and patient-specific order particulars
Submit the checked final test order to the diagnostic department
Retrieve the diagnostic results and verify their patient and specimen context
Interpret diagnostic results in the patient's clinical circumstances
Record the diagnostic interpretation and required follow-up in the patient record

tasks.design: Configure native patient, order and result views in {OTHER}, the electronic health record, and linked testing references in {DOCS}. Keep test selection and interpretation with the midwife, separate the actual clinical order submission, and use a native template for the interpretation note.
tasks.previous_blocker: Patient context, order particulars and result notes require repeated navigation and entry.
tasks.enabler_now: Native order favourites, result views and documentation templates can reduce supporting work.
tasks.still_hard: Clinical indication, specimen context and result significance require professional judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Select appropriate tests and interpret results in the patient's circumstances.

ambition.what: Recognise missing result context earlier without delegating clinical interpretation.

tasks.altitude: Keep clinical decisions accountable while simplifying their supporting record work.

reach.learn: Preserve patient, specimen and result provenance.

evidence.claim: Native clinical order favourites, result views and interpretation templates could reduce supporting work; the midwifery saving is an E1 scenario.

assumptions: OTHER means the electronic health record. The diagnostic department is inside the organisation; its order is consequential and checked when submitted, unlike an ordinary author save.

The midwife produces patient ID, selected test, indication, specimen particulars and timing in s3, retaining eight hours; missing details require manual resolution. Existing result records are produced by the diagnostic department, and patient and specimen verification is counted in s5.
The midwife writes interpretation and follow-up fields in s7, retaining 10.5 hours. No machine interprets results, decides tests or issues an unreviewed order.
Native favourites, views and note headings come first. The future keeps ordinary record save time within entry, with no save-only saving or author approval stage.
unknowns: Current order configuration and compatibility of external diagnostic results.
research_questions: Can native views and templates reduce total order and documentation effort after patient and specimen checks?

incremental.description: Maintain order favourites and interpretation templates.

approvals.approved_version: Exact final test order, patient, indication, specimen particulars and destination; changes require renewed submission-time checking.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central E1 case: B=100, R=88.5, gross=11.5; upkeep=2 gives net=9.5. Conservative case: incompatible result views and unusual orders leave lookup and entry unchanged, while the note template retains 12 of 15 hours; R=97, net=1. With a usable result view and seven total supporting hours saved, net=5. Selection, order submission and interpretation retain 50 hours.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Capture physical examination findings and produce an accurate patient record entry.

steps.what: Verify the patient record and locate the physical examination documentation context
Capture the actual physical examination findings and their relevant qualifications
Enter structured examination findings using the applicable native record template
Write the narrative explanation of the physical examination findings

loop.purpose: Draft an examination narrative from findings explicitly captured by the midwife.
loop.input: Captured observations, qualifications and structured entry.
loop.output: Narrative draft retaining negatives, uncertainty and source anchors.
loop.check: Midwife compares every finding and qualification with captured observations; unperformed examinations must never be described as normal.
loop.stop: One correction pass; unreliable or unsupported text is written manually.
loop.why_not_simpler: Native fields and headings help routine entries but cannot express all qualified free-text findings.

steps.what: Check and correct the examination entry for accuracy and omissions
Save the completed examination entry in the same patient record

tasks.design: Use native examination fields in {OTHER}, the electronic health record, before adding bounded narrative drafting from explicitly captured findings. The midwife checks and corrects the entry, then saves it in the same record without an added author approval stage.
tasks.previous_blocker: Actual findings must be turned into structured entries and qualified narrative prose.
tasks.enabler_now: Native templates and source-bounded drafting can support the separate documentation work.
tasks.still_hard: A missing qualification or invented normal finding can mislead later care.
tasks.human_edge: Preserve exactly what was examined, observed and uncertain.
tasks.altitude: Make examination documentation accurate with less repeated composition.

reach.learn: Distinguish observed findings from unexamined or uncertain areas.

evidence.claim: Autoscriber drafts consultation notes for clinician validation in electronic records; that supports a documentation capability, not autonomous examination or a midwifery-specific saving.
The digest describes a large clinician note evaluation with self-estimated documentation time improvements and retained editing; its setting does not establish this task's saving.

assumptions: OTHER means the electronic health record. Physical examination itself is a separate clinical activity; this task owns its complete documentation, including capture, structured entry, prose, corrections and save.

The midwife produces patient and encounter context, actual findings, examination scope, negatives and qualifications in s2 with all 25 hours retained. Missing or unclear observations are resolved manually; the loop cannot infer a normal finding.
Try native fields and headings first. Narrative review retains 15 hours in s4, final checking retains 14 and the ordinary same-system save retains its one small hour with no approval or saving.
No ambient recording or hidden write-back is assumed; the loop uses the midwife's explicitly captured observations.
unknowns: Native examination template coverage and frequency of qualified findings.
research_questions: Does narrative drafting reduce total documentation after checking for invented normal findings and omitted qualifications?

already_counted.description: Review and correct the examination narrative draft.

incremental.description: Maintain examination fields and audit drafting errors.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central E1 task scenario: B=100, R=83.75, gross=16.25; upkeep=4 gives net=12.25. Conservative case: poor template fit retains all 25 structured-entry hours and narrative correction retains 19 of 25 hours, R=94, net=2. With partial template fit, eleven combined composition hours saved give net=7. Capture, identity checking, final correction and save remain 50 hours.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare appropriate care education, explain it to patients and families, and record the discussion.

steps.what: Clarify the patient's and family members' care education needs and concerns
Retrieve vetted prenatal, intrapartum, postpartum, newborn or interconception care materials
Prepare a patient-specific education outline and select suitable handouts
Educate patients and family members and check understanding through discussion
Provide the checked handouts to the patient and authorised family recipients
Record the education given, understanding and remaining questions in the patient record

tasks.design: Configure vetted education collections and outline headings in {DOCS}, plus a native education record in {OTHER}, the electronic health record. The midwife adapts and explains the material, checks understanding and separately provides the selected handouts.
tasks.previous_blocker: Suitable materials and education record headings are repeatedly assembled.
tasks.enabler_now: Vetted reference collections and native fields can support preparation and recording.
tasks.still_hard: The patient's circumstances, fears and understanding shape safe education.
tasks.human_edge: Explain sensitively, notice misunderstanding and respond to individual questions.

ambition.what: Prepare appropriate material for a family with different language or accessibility needs, subject to available vetted content.

tasks.altitude: Keep education personal while simplifying supporting preparation and documentation.

reach.learn: Use the recorded understanding and unresolved questions.

evidence.claim: The digest identifies Thuisarts as guideline-based patient information; this supports using vetted texts, not autonomous patient-specific advice.
Native reference collections, outline headings and education fields could reduce supporting effort; the estimated saving is E1.

assumptions: OTHER means the electronic health record. The scenario includes an existing education outline and education record, separately priced from the live discussion.

The midwife identifies needs in s1, selects references in s2, writes the tailored outline in s3 with 12 retained hours, and captures topics, recipients, materials, understanding and unresolved questions in s6 with seven retained hours. Missing or unsuitable material requires manual preparation.

Native views, headings and vetted handouts come first; no chatbot or generated clinical advice is proposed. Final content and recipient suitability are checked within the real patient communication and handout provision, without an additional approval meeting.
Ordinary internal note saves have no self-gate and contribute no separate saving.
unknowns: Availability of vetted language and accessibility variants.
research_questions: Does an indexed material collection reduce preparation after checking patient-specific suitability?

already_counted.description: Record education, understanding and unresolved questions.

incremental.description: Maintain vetted education collections and record fields.

approvals.approved_version: Each exact patient-specific explanation and response is checked for current applicability before it is expressed.
Exact handout edition, patient suitability and authorised recipients; changed materials or recipients require a fresh provision-time check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central E1 case: B=100, R=92, gross=8; upkeep=2 yields net=6. Conservative case: no suitable language template and nonstandard education records leave preparation and writing unchanged; indexed retrieval saves two hours, R=98 and net=0. A usable outline that saves three more hours gives net=3. Live needs discussion, education and actual handout provision retain 65 hours.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Write and communicate checked patient summaries to other care providers.

steps.what: Select current patient information and verify the care summary context
Write the patient summary brief and identify essential handover points
Draft the narrative medical summary from selected records and the midwife's brief

loop.purpose: Draft a care summary expressing the midwife's chosen handover information.
loop.input: Written summary brief and selected current record passages.
loop.output: Narrative summary draft with source anchors and explicit gaps.
loop.check: Midwife verifies chronology, medications, qualifications and handover relevance against the selected records.
loop.stop: One revision; unresolved contradictions or unreliable passages require manual writing.
loop.why_not_simpler: A fixed summary template cannot express all case-specific chronology and qualified clinical facts.

steps.what: Check and correct the medical summary against the patient record
Save the completed summary in the same medical record
Communicate the checked patient summary to the receiving care provider

tasks.design: Configure a current-record view and summary headings in {OTHER}, the electronic health record, then draft from the midwife's explicit brief and selected evidence. Separate correction, the small same-system save and the real provider handover; retain the handover conversation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Current information and case-specific narrative must be selected and rewritten for each handover.
tasks.enabler_now: Native record views and bounded narrative drafting can support summary preparation.
tasks.still_hard: Stale information and omitted qualifications can misdirect the receiving clinician.
tasks.human_edge: Choose clinically relevant information and ensure the receiving provider understands it.

ambition.what: Spot contradictory current information while preparing handovers.

tasks.altitude: Use summaries to improve continuity rather than repeat record prose.

reach.learn: Check unresolved issues and source dates.

evidence.claim: Juvoly drafts referral letters; this is an adjacent drafting capability, not proof of this handover saving.

assumptions: OTHER means the electronic health record. This scenario is a summary for a colleague inside the organisation, so its communication has internal authority. A provider outside the organisation would require external authority and recipient permissions.

The midwife selects current source passages in s1 with 16 retained hours, then produces the patient identity, handover purpose, essential clinical points, source dates and unresolved issues in s2 with all 15 hours counted. Missing or contradictory facts require manual reconciliation.
This task owns the cross-episode summary rather than rewriting examination notes already priced in the examination documentation task.

Try native views and summary headings first. The one-hour same-system save remains fully retained and ungated; the actual provider communication checks its final summary and recipient within its 15 retained hours.
unknowns: Current record metadata quality and summary reuse across care episodes.
research_questions: Does bounded summary drafting reduce total work after stale information and omitted qualifications are corrected?

already_counted.description: Review and correct the narrative summary draft.

incremental.description: Maintain summary headings and audit source and chronology errors.

approvals.approved_version: Exact corrected summary, essential handover points and receiving provider; changes require a fresh communication-time check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central E1 case: B=100, R=82, gross=18; upkeep=5 yields net=13. Conservative case: stale source metadata leaves selection at 20 hours and correction-heavy drafting at 28 of 35 hours; R=93, net=2. When a current-record view saves three hours and drafting retains 25 hours, R=87 and net=8. Brief capture, final correction, save and actual handover retain 45 hours.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Keep clinical decisions and patient communication with the midwife while improving their supporting documentation.
reach: Connect accurate examination and diagnostic records with patient education and provider continuity.
role.ambitious_version: A nurse midwife who keeps personal clinical judgement and communication while producing clearer, timely and traceable records.
